result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of difference—the fear that divides people into "us" and "them," that fuels prejudice, conflict, and systemic injustice. I would replace it with a universal curiosity, a deep and abiding wonder at the vast spectrum of human experience, and a commitment to understanding before judgment.

This wouldn’t erase conflict entirely, but it would make empathy the default response rather than the exception. It would mean that no child grows up believing their identity is a threat, that no community is forced to justify its existence, and that no system is built on the dehumanization of others.

It’s not a simple fix—fear is deeply ingrained—but if I had to choose one thing, this is it. Because once fear loses its grip, everything else becomes possible.
